problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t)=\frac{{t}^{2}}{{t}^{2}+1}.$ Calculate the velocity at time $t.$

feedback.worked_solution:
The velocity is the derivative of the position function $x(t)$ with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}+{e}^{t})) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}+{e}^{t})\cdot (3{t}^{2}+{e}^{t}) \\  & =-2(3{t}^{2}+{e}^{t})\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}+{e}^{t})\end{aligned}
$$
